circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island designed by Hermann Tilke, has served as the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. It represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One circuits, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track that encircles Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year along with various supporting racing categories. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 classification, confirming its suitability for top-level motorsport competition.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit has a storied history hosting the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct periods, first as the Österreichring from 1970-1987 and later as the A1-Ring following its reconstruction and abbreviation from 1997-2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track positioned along Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan, spanning 6. 003 km to rank as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before transitioning to become the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the 5. 412 km Bahrain International Circuit hosts the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, which made history as the Middle East's inaugural F1 race. The FIA Grade 1 facility accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2 Series and endurance racing, with multiple circuit configurations available for different events.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a diverse mix of straights and corners that test multiple aspects of driver skill and car performance. The venue, which holds FIA Grade 1 status, accommodates over 140,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This Belgian circuit spanning over 7 kilometres has been a staple of Formula One since 1950, when it hosted a race during the championship's inaugural season. Located near the town of Spa in Wallonia, the track has served as the permanent home of the Belgian Grand Prix annually from 1985 onwards, with only brief absences in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometer temporary street circuit that annually hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various motorsporting series including world sportscar championships, open-wheel racing, and North American touring car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit is a racing venue located in Jiading, Shanghai, China, most notable for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix from 2004 to 2019 before returning to the calendar in 2024. In addition to the Formula One race, the facility began accommodating electric racing competitions from 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located in England between the Northamptonshire settlements of Silverstone and Whittlebury, this racing venue has served as the primary home of the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably staged the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After sharing hosting duties with Aintree and Brands Hatch during the 1955-1986 period, the circuit became the permanent base for Britain's Formula One event from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became the setting for Formula One's first grand prix held within the Eastern Bloc when it hosted the Hungarian Grand Prix in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One circuit, the 4. 381 km track was constructed outside the city near a highway after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's main park were rejected.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located north of Milan in Italy, Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 that ranks among the world's earliest purpose-built racing venues and remains Europe's oldest on the mainland. The venue has hosted the Italian Grand Prix nearly continuously since 1949, making it one of only four circuits with an unbroken presence on the Formula One calendar from the sport's beginning, and its long straights and rapid corners have earned it the nickname "Temple of Speed.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km motorsport facility in Mie Prefecture, Japan, operated by Honda Mobilityland. The track, which accommodates 155,000 spectators, serves as a premier venue for Formula One racing and the Japanese Super Formula championship.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a temporary street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, weaving past the city's most famous hotels and entertainment venues along Las Vegas Boulevard. The layout incorporates iconic landmarks such as the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it winds through the urban landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honors two deceased racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in motorsport accidents in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The circuit has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix across multiple eras, most recently from 2015 onwards on its current layout, following earlier hosting periods that concluded in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design, it was purpose-built for the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: Monaco's street circuit winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, measuring 3. 337 kilometers around the harbor area. The track is officially known by the Monte Carlo name, reflecting that most of its layout occupies the Monte Carlo neighborhood within the principality.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km Dutch racing circuit situated in coastal dunes west of Amsterdam that hosted Formula One's Dutch Grand Prix following its return to the calendar in 2021. The venue held this status until the partnership concluded after 2026, with the track operating under a sponsorship designation since mid-2025.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits north of Doha in Qatar and spans 5. 419 kilometers with a prominent 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise circuit that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace, who tragically died in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The venue hosts major international motorsport events and features additional facilities including a karting track dedicated to another Brazilian racing legend.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along the Saudi Arabian coastline beside the Red Sea. Since 2021, it has been the home of Formula One's Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, and it began hosting a Formula E event in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown area and adjacent neighborhoods, forming a temporary racing venue around the Marina Bay waterfront.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced mix of straightaways and varied corner types that test all aspects of driver and vehicle performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA facility that serves as the primary venue for the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts multiple major motorsport series including MotoGP and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, along with various other national and international racing competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a dual Thai and British racing driver who currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Fernando Alonso is a Spanish driver currently racing for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 alongside 32 career Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, he has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories with Toyota and the 2018–19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have won both a Formula One world title and a World Endurance Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed eight victories since beginning his career in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, bringing his talents to the grid in the premier motorsport category.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto, a Brazilian motorsport competitor, currently races in Formula One representing Audi.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas has secured ten Grand Prix victories during his 13-year Formula One career and currently races for Cadillac. He achieved consecutive runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while competing for Mercedes in 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine, representing his country in the sport's top motorsport series.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan holds a reserve role with Haas in Formula One while primarily competing in European Le Mans Series prototypes for Nielsen Racing. He has made limited Formula One appearances, contesting seven races across the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently competing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri remains a significant achievement in his racing career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver currently racing for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, competing under the French flag.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has secured seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple all-time records in the sport, including the most career victories, pole positions, and podium finishes.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved significant success in endurance racing by securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 alongside Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently driving for Racing Bulls in Formula One competition.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 championship standings. Over his nine seasons in the sport, he has claimed nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, the Danish driver known as K-Mag, transitioned from Formula One competition spanning 2014-2020 and 2022-2024 to compete primarily in the World Endurance Championship with BMW through WRT. He supplements this racing program with a part-time NASCAR Cup Series campaign, piloting the No. 91 Chevrolet for Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship and has secured 13 race victories over his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently competing for Haas. The racer achieved a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian round while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican driver, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One. The 15-season veteran finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian driver competing in Formula One with McLaren, having accumulated nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-year career in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-year career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant, an American driver, competed in Formula One during the 2023-2024 seasons before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, following previous stints in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently competing in Formula One with the Aston Martin team.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, holds a reserve role with both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls. After competing full-time in Formula One between 2021 and 2025, he transitioned to a backup position for the 2026 season.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen has claimed four consecutive Formula One World Drivers' Championships between 2021 and 2024 while racing for Red Bull Racing under the Dutch flag. With 73 Grand Prix victories accumulated over 12 seasons, he stands among Formula One's most successful competitors in the sport's modern era.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a Formula One driver, currently holding a reserve position at Cadillac after competing in the series from 2022 through 2024. He remains the sole Chinese-born driver to have participated in Formula One competition.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed under the Alpine banner since 2021, serving as Renault's official works entry until the manufacturer's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025. Previously operating as Renault F1 Team, the squad was rebranded to represent the French carmaker's Alpine sports car division. BWT Alpine carried forward the facility's established presence in Formula One under new automotive sponsorship.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British manufacturer, has competed in Formula One through multiple incarnations, with the current racing operation run by AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the motorsport arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, stands as the sport's most storied and victorious outfit, competing continuously since the inaugural 1950 World Championship. Nicknamed after their iconic emblem, the team has maintained an unbroken presence throughout Formula One's entire history while accumulating more championship success than any other competitor.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, debuting on the grid in 2016. Following Guenther Steiner's departure in January 2024, Ayao Komatsu assumed the role of team principal and continues to lead the outfit.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Sauber was a Swiss motorsport engineering company established in 1970 that progressed from building sports cars to becoming a Formula One constructor. The team competed in F1 from 1993 until 2025, establishing itself as the sport's fourth-longest-serving constructor, while previously excelling in endurance racing including a Le Mans victory and two world championships. Audi acquired the organization and its operations in 2024 to serve as the foundation for its own Formula One program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One competitor headquartered at its state-of-the-art facility in Woking, Surrey. The team operates as a division of the McLaren Group, with full ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, based in Brackley and operating under a German licence, represents the latest iteration of Mercedes' involvement in Formula One dating back to 1954. The team adopted a tri-ownership structure in 2022 when Ineos joined Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff as equal stakeholders. Mercedes-branded racing efforts are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows".

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls competes as a Formula One constructor and team representing Italy since 2024, operating alongside Red Bull Racing as one of two F1 entities owned by Red Bull GmbH. Headquartered in Faenza with operations near Milton Keynes, the team functions as a sister squad within the Red Bull organization's competitive structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team operates as a sister outfit to Red Bull Racing within the same corporate structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England but licensed under Austria, represents one of two Formula One entries owned by the Red Bull beverage conglomerate. Established in 2005, the team was led by Christian Horner for two decades before Laurent Mekies assumed the leadership role in 2025. The squad competes alongside the conglomerate's second Formula One outfit, Racing Bulls.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, Williams is a British Formula One team and constructor headquartered in Grove, Oxfordshire. The team emerged following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture and has established itself as a significant force in the sport's history.
